nodes.label: Quantium Crew Website
nodes.rationale: Positioned as a marketing site for a proactive strategic technology partner rather than reactive IT support, so the whole information architecture leads a visitor from problem framing to engagement CTA.

nodes.label: Hero Section
nodes.rationale: Headline 'We don't fix technology. We engineer it.' is the core positioning claim; dual CTA (free tech assessment / explore solutions) splits high-intent from browsing visitors.

nodes.label: Problem / Value Proposition Section
nodes.rationale: Frames fragmented business systems as the pain so the four-division offering reads as consolidation rather than upsell.

nodes.label: Services / Divisions Module
nodes.rationale: Four named divisions under one brand support the 'one-stop tech partner' claim: a single contract instead of five vendors.

nodes.label: Why Quantium Crew Module
nodes.rationale: Differentiators chosen are startup mindset, fast execution and scalability rather than price, to avoid competing with commodity IT support vendors.

nodes.label: How We Work (5-Step Process)
nodes.rationale: Analyze, Design, Build, Optimize, Support — ends on Support so the engagement is framed as ongoing rather than project-terminal.

nodes.label: Visitor Scroll Flow
nodes.rationale: Sections are ordered as a persuasion funnel (hook, problem, capability, differentiation, process, proof, ask) so a single scroll performs the whole sales narrative without navigation.

nodes.label: No User Authentication Required
nodes.rationale: All content is public because the site is purely a marketing surface; this original decision is later contradicted by the shipped Supabase admin/chat auth model.

nodes.label: Dark + Electric Accent Design Style
nodes.rationale: Black/dark-gray base with electric blue (#00D4FF) or violet (#8B5CF6) accents, minimalist line icons and explicitly no generic stock tech imagery, to read as an engineering firm rather than a reseller.

nodes.label: Email Service Integration (EmailJS)
nodes.rationale: Contact form submissions are pushed to a third-party email service so the site can stay fully static with no server-side processing.

nodes.label: No Backend / No Data Model
nodes.rationale: Declared explicitly: no API, no server architecture, no database, because the original scope was a static marketing site. Superseded in practice by the Supabase backend described in the README.

nodes.label: Single-Route SPA (/ only)
nodes.rationale: Only '/' was specified, with every section on one page; the shipped site instead exposes /contact, /team, /testimonials, /privacy, /terms and /services/*.

nodes.label: Contact Page Separation
nodes.rationale: Contact was pulled out of the single-page scroll onto a dedicated /contact route so the primary CTAs ('Get Started', 'Schedule Assessment') have a real destination.

nodes.label: Multi-Language Internationalization
nodes.rationale: English, Spanish, Portuguese, French and Chinese with browser-language auto-detection, driven by a single translation dictionary covering every section.

nodes.label: Luxury Minimalist Visual Polish
nodes.rationale: Glassmorphic hover on use-case cards, background imagery with overlay on the problem section, grid pattern plus glow/scale on service cards, all tuned toward an 'Apple-style' premium feel.

nodes.label: Supabase Backend (Data, Auth, Storage)
nodes.rationale: The site outgrew its static-marketing scope: testimonials, client chat and image upload all needed persistence, so Supabase supplies database, auth and storage without standing up a custom server.

nodes.label: RLS Permission Model
nodes.rationale: Authorization is enforced in the database, not the frontend: new testimonials are forced to 'pending' by RLS rather than by client code, so a tampered browser cannot self-approve content.

nodes.label: testimonials Storage Bucket
nodes.rationale: Public bucket capped at 5MB and restricted to images so anonymous submitters can attach a photo without opening an arbitrary-file upload path.

nodes.label: Anonymous Client Chat Session
nodes.rationale: Chat visitors get a Supabase anonymous session rather than a login, which still yields a stable JWT identity so RLS can scope them to their own conversation and force sender='client'.

nodes.label: Admin Role via app_metadata Claim
nodes.rationale: Admin is decided by app_metadata.role='admin' in the JWT and deliberately NOT user_metadata, because users can edit their own user_metadata and would be able to self-promote to admin.

nodes.label: SECURITY DEFINER Welcome-Message Trigger
nodes.rationale: The chat welcome message must appear to come from 'admin', but RLS forbids the browser from writing admin-sender rows, so a SECURITY DEFINER trigger inserts it server-side instead.

nodes.label: Anonymous Sign-Ins Dashboard Setting
nodes.rationale: Cannot be applied by migration; if left off the client chat never starts, making it a required manual out-of-band deploy step.

nodes.label: Hand-Maintained database.ts Types
nodes.rationale: src/types/database.ts is deliberately not generated: status, priority and sender are text columns with CHECK constraints, which `supabase gen types` emits as plain `string`; hand-writing them narrows the types to literal unions.

nodes.label: @react-three/drei v9 Version Pin
nodes.rationale: Pinned to ^9.x on purpose: drei v10 requires @react-three/fiber@9, which requires React 19, while this project is on React 18. Upgrading drei therefore forces a React major migration first.

nodes.label: Consolidated Permissive Policies Migration
nodes.rationale: 20260813031228_consolidate_permissive_policies.sql is named as the single source of truth for the final RLS policy state, so readers do not have to replay the whole migration history.

nodes.label: SPA Root Mount Point
nodes.rationale: Single #root div hydrated by /src/main.tsx as an ES module — the standard Vite SPA entry shape.

nodes.label: Vite HMR Error Reporter
nodes.rationale: Inline module subscribes to the 'vite:error' HMR event and logs message plus code frame to the console, so build errors surface in the browser console during development.

nodes.label: Homepage Accessibility Snapshot (13:47)
nodes.rationale: Playwright accessibility-tree capture of the shipped Spanish homepage, used as the ground truth of what actually renders versus what the PRD specified.

nodes.label: Rack Elevation Metaphor (4U/3U/2U/1U)
nodes.rationale: The four divisions are visually mapped onto a server rack elevation — Cloud/4U (Dev), Server/3U (Systems), Network/2U (Support+), Floor/1U (Install) — which literalises the tagline 'del cableado a la nube' and makes the one-vendor-whole-stack claim legible at a glance instead of using generic stock imagery.

nodes.label: Six-Phase Methodology (shipped)
nodes.rationale: Descubrimiento, Estrategia, Implementacion, Testing & QA, Lanzamiento, Soporte Continuo — each phase carries a duration estimate and named deliverables, sold as 'cero sorpresas' transparency.

nodes.label: Strategic Technology Partners Marquee
nodes.rationale: Ubiquiti, Cisco, Proxmox, Lenovo, Dell, HP, VMware, AWS, Google Cloud, Fortinet, Intel and NVIDIA are repeated three times in the DOM to build a seamless looping scroll marquee.

nodes.label: Spec-Plate Animated Stats
nodes.rationale: Clients, projects, years and satisfaction are styled as a hardware spec plate ('QCREW - PA') and all read 0 in the snapshot, indicating count-up animation that had not yet run at capture time.

nodes.label: Work-Order Styled CTA
nodes.rationale: The final CTA is dressed as a service work order ('Paso 1 de 3') with explicit Alcance / Entrega / Costo terms — written proposal in 48h, free, no commitment — reducing perceived risk of clicking.

nodes.label: Shipped Site Route Map
nodes.rationale: Live routes are /, /contact, /team, /testimonials, /privacy, /terms and /services/{dev,systems,support,install} — far beyond the single '/' the architecture document specified.

nodes.label: Placeholder Footer Contact Details
nodes.rationale: Footer still ships template data — phone +1 (555) 123-4567 and address '123 Tech Boulevard, Innovation District, CA 94043' — contradicting the Panama positioning stated in the hero and copyright line. Social links also point at '#'.

nodes.label: Homepage Accessibility Snapshot (13:48)
nodes.rationale: Captured 60 seconds after the 13:47 snapshot and structurally identical apart from Playwright ref-id prefixes (f29 -> f30); the stat counters still read 0, suggesting the count-up never fires in this capture path.

nodes.label: Company Type Selection (Agent Design)
nodes.rationale: The company type is asked first because it determines how many AI agents are needed and what responsibility each one carries.

nodes.label: Option C: Quantium Crew as the Modeled Company
nodes.rationale: Proposes designing the agents around real in-house projects (CAMCARD_SALUD, RRHH MENU, Findwork) rather than a generic template, so the agent roles map to work that already exists.
nodes.norm_label: option c: quantium crew as the modeled company

nodes.label: Agent Autonomy Spectrum
nodes.rationale: Defines what 'vida propia' means as a four-point autonomy ladder; options are explicitly combinable, so autonomy is treated as composable traits rather than mutually exclusive tiers.

nodes.label: Proactive Agent with Alerts
nodes.rationale: Monitors its own domain and pushes warnings unprompted (example: cash runway dropping below three months).

nodes.label: Autonomous Agent with Routines
nodes.rationale: Owns a schedule, emits automatic reports, makes micro-decisions and coordinates agent-to-agent without human mediation (Sales forecast handed to Finance every Monday 9am).

nodes.label: Agent with Personality and Memory
nodes.rationale: Named role with a distinct voice plus recall of prior conversations, so the agent reads as a colleague rather than a tool.
